series.$note: series.observed holds several sources and must not be read as one curve. DS-35: All greenhouse gases including land-use change, GWP100 (OWID, from Climate Watch / PIK), from 1990. DS-02: Asset-level observed emissions, CO₂e GWP100 (Climate TRACE); land use accounted differently from OWID, 2015-2025. DS-40: Total GHG emissions including LULUCF/LUCF exactly as the Party submitted them to the UNFCCC, on that Party’s own reporting guidelines and GWP set (UNFCCC Data Interface, snapshot of 2024-07-05). Non-Annex I Parties report only the years their national communications cover, and the figure is negative where reported removals exceed reported emissions. Points from an NDC document are that document's own inventory basis. The same year can appear more than once with different values; R3 keeps them side by side and never averages them.

derived.$note: Trend: least-squares slope over 35 observed years (1990-2024) from DS-35, compared against the DS-06-NDC target of 1528.524 MtCO₂e by 2030. The two are not necessarily on the same inventory scope, see series.$note. The target tonnage is derived here, not quoted: 50% below DS-35's 2005 value of 3057.048 MtCO₂e. The document states the percentage; the level it is applied to comes from DS-35, on DS-35's inventory scope, which is not necessarily the document's.
derived.$reason: observed emissions are rising by 2.37 MtCO₂e/yr while the target requires a fall of 212.65 MtCO₂e/yr. No multiple of the current trend reaches it, so no finite gap factor is reported.

evidence.sentence: BRAZIL'S NDC TARGET FOR 2035 After a careful process involving analysis and consultation with federal ministries within the Interministerial Committee on Climate Change (CIM), Brazil is setting an economy-wide target of reducing its net greenhouse gas emissions by 59 to 67 percent below 2005 levels by 2035, which is consistent, in absolute terms, with an emission level of 1.05 to 0.85 GtCO2e, according to the most recent inventory data.

(d) Target relative to the reference indicator, expressed numerically, for example in percentage or amount of reduction; The target for 2035 is a reduction on the range of 59 to 67 per cent compared to 2005 emissions, which is consistent with a reduction of 1.51 to 1.71 GtCO2e, according to the latest inventory data.

BRAZIL'S NDC -National determination to contribute and transform (g) The intention to use voluntary cooperation under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, if applicable: The Government of Brazil estimates that it is possible to raise the ambition of its national mitigation actions beyond the base level of 59 percent below 2005 levels by 2035 or 1.05 GtCO2e, as proposed in section 1b, through the international transfer of mitigation results (ITMOs) generated in its territory.

title.text: 4. Structured summary: Tracking progress made in implementing and achieving the NDC under Article 4 of the Paris Agreement a

progress.text: Brazil is progressing towards the NDC target. The total GHG emissions decreased in 2022, compared to the GHG emission level in the NDC base year (2005). In 2020, emissions decreased significantly to 1.82 Gt CO₂ eq, mainly in the LULUCF sector, related to the reduction in deforestation, which was due above all to the adoption of Action Plans for the Prevention and Control of Deforestation and Fires. Despite the increase in national emissions in 2021 (explained in Section 3.1, NIR 2024), Brazil reverted the growth trend in 2022, registering emissions of 2.04 Gt CO₂ eq.

verdict.text: Brazil pledges a 50% reduction by 2030 against 2005 baseline (condition not read). The registry's current submission for this Party is Second Nationally Determined Contribution, filed 2024-11-13. It was read and refused, so the figure above comes from the First NDC (2022). 73 observed values are loaded from DS-02 (11), DS-35 (35), DS-40 (27). For 2024 the sources disagree: DS-35 2804.4 MtCO₂e, DS-02 1138.1 MtCO₂e. They are on different inventory scopes and the engine does not reconcile them. The target is not reached on the observed trend. Both figures are on DS-35's inventory: the document's percentage applied to DS-35's 2005 level, not the document's own. It submitted BTR1. 4 of 8 components have been confirmed in the document; the rest are unparsed, which is not a finding against the country. ND-GAIN scores it 50.7 for 2024. In the first NDC round, WRI's CAIT assessment recorded: Reduce GHG emissions by 37% in 2025, and by 43% (indicative) in 2030 below 2005 levels It was classed unconditional. That is a 2016 assessment of an earlier submission, not the target above. Projected warming for 2080-2099 against 1995-2014 ranges from +1.15°C under SSP1-2.6 to +4.49°C under SSP5-8.5. These are model runs, not observations.
